Analytic torsion

Words: 49
Differential geometry OurBigBook.com
Analytic torsion is a spectral invariant constructed from regularized determinants of the Laplacians on differential forms with suitable flat coefficients. It is the analytic counterpart of combinatorial Reidemeister torsion, whose refinements include Turaev torsion; equality theorems relate the spectral and combinatorial invariants under appropriate hypotheses on the manifold and coefficients.

Differential geometry of surfaces

Words: 25
Differential geometry OurBigBook.com
The differential geometry of smooth smooth surfaces studies their induced Riemannian metrics and intrinsic or extrinsic curvature. The first fundamental form measures lengths, while the second fundamental form and shape operator describe bending in an ambient space.

Pullback (differential geometry, f∗)

Words: 32
Differential geometry OurBigBook.com
A smooth map between manifolds f:M→N pulls a function back by composition and pulls a covariant tensor back by applying its differential to each vector argument. The pullback of a differential form is the alternating-tensor case and commutes with the exterior derivative.

Laplace operators in differential geometry

Words: 26
Differential geometry OurBigBook.com
This family includes the Laplace-Beltrami operator on functions, the Hodge Laplacian on differential forms, and the rough Laplacian associated with a connection on a vector bundle. Their domains and sign conventions must be specified when comparing them.

Critical point of a smooth map (rankdfx​<dimY)

Words: 57 Articles: 1
Differential geometry OurBigBook.com
For a smooth map f:X→Y, a critical point is a point where its differential is not surjective. This is relative to the target dimension: it is not in general equivalent to a derivative being zero.

Critical value (f(xc​))

Words: 24
Critical point of a smooth map OurBigBook.com
A critical value is the image of at least one critical point of a smooth map. A regular value has no critical point in its fiber. Values outside the image are regular vacuously.

Calibrated geometry

Words: 248 Articles: 5
Differential geometry OurBigBook.com
Calibrated geometry constructs volume-minimizing submanifolds through closed differential forms with a tangent-plane bound. It gives an algebraic sufficient condition for solving the nonlinear minimal surface problem.

Generalized calibration

Words: 64
Calibrated geometry OurBigBook.com
A generalized calibration bounds the full energy of a supersymmetric brane, including its potential or gauge couplings. For a membrane, compatible spinor bilinears obey dΩ=ιK​F. In a stationary gauge LK​A=0, Cartan's magic formula proves d(Ω+ιK​A)=0. The closed charge form then supplies the energy bound. This extends ordinary calibration from volume alone to charged branes, as developed in Topological charges for branes in M-theory.

Calibrated submanifold (φ∣Σ​=volΣ​)

Words: 70 Articles: 1
Calibrated geometry OurBigBook.com
An oriented submanifold is calibrated by a calibration when its tangent planes attain the comass bound at every point. Closedness then compares its volume with homologous competitors by Stokes theorem.

Calibration implies volume minimization (Vol(Σ)≤Vol(Σ′))

Words: 42
Calibrated submanifold OurBigBook.com
If Σ is calibrated by φ and Σ′ is homologous with the same boundary, Stokes theorem gives ∫Σ​φ=∫Σ′​φ. The tangent-plane bound gives ∫Σ′​φ≤Vol(Σ′), while calibration gives ∫Σ​φ=Vol(Σ). Thus Σ minimizes volume in its relative homology class and is a minimal submanifold wherever smooth.

Calibration (differential geometry, dφ=0,∥φ∥∗​≤1)

Words: 92 Articles: 1
Calibrated geometry OurBigBook.com
A calibration is a closed real differential form whose comass is at most one. Restricting it to any oriented unit tangent plane therefore gives at most that plane's volume. A calibrated submanifold attains equality everywhere, and calibration implies volume minimization among homologous competitors.

Spinor calibration form (φab​=ϵ†Γ0​Γab​ϵ)

Words: 58
Calibration (differential geometry) OurBigBook.com
In a flux-free static supergravity background with a parallel unit Killing spinor, this two-form satisfies the membrane tangent-plane bound because Γ0​γ(u)γ(v) is a Hermitian involution. Its eigenvalues are ±1, so φ(u,v)≤1, with equality precisely at the kappa symmetry projector condition. Parallel transport gives ∇φ=0 and hence dφ=0. This constructs an ordinary calibration; flux backgrounds instead call for a generalized calibration.

Carnot-Carathéodory distance (dCC​(g,h)=infγ​∫∣x˙t​∣dt)

Words: 120 Articles: 1
Differential geometry OurBigBook.com
On a graded nilpotent Lie group whose first layer generates its Lie algebra, a horizontal curve obeys γ˙​t​=(Lγt​​)∗​x˙t​ for a control in the first layer. The displayed infimum is over horizontal curves with prescribed endpoints. The distance is left invariant and homogeneous under the graded dilations. On a free nilpotent Lie group it measures the least Euclidean length of a path realizing a prescribed truncated path signature.

Chow-Rashevskii theorem

Words: 58
Carnot-Carathéodory distance OurBigBook.com
On a connected manifold, a smooth bracket-generating family of vector fields connects every pair of points by a piecewise smooth horizontal curve. For a free step-N nilpotent Lie group, this says that every group element is the path signature of a sufficiently regular path. In the planar step-two case, a closed rectangle prescribes the signed area and a following straight segment prescribes the displacement.

Hodge theory

Words: 490 Articles: 10
Differential geometry OurBigBook.com
Hodge theory connects de Rham cohomology with harmonic differential forms through the Hodge Laplacian on a compact Riemannian manifold. The Hodge decomposition theorem supplies a unique harmonic representative of each cohomology class. On a compact Kähler manifold, the decomposition additionally respects the complex bidegrees of differential forms.

Hodge structure (HC​=⨁p+q=w​Hp,q)

Words: 457 Articles: 9
Hodge theory OurBigBook.com
A pure integral Hodge structure is a finite-rank free abelian group with a complex decomposition satisfying Hp,q=Hq,p and p+q=w. The integer w is its weight. Its equivalent Hodge filtration is Fp=⨁r≥p​Hr,w−r.

Variation of Hodge structure (∇Fp⊆Fp−1⊗ΩS1​)

Words: 137 Articles: 2
Hodge structure OurBigBook.com
A pure integral variation consists of a local system of free abelian groups, holomorphic filtration subbundles of its associated flat bundle, and fibrewise Hodge structures of fixed weight and Hodge numbers. Its flat connection satisfies Griffiths transversality. A polarized variation additionally has a flat integral bilinear form polarizing every fibre.
Griffiths transversality (∇Fp⊆Fp−1⊗ΩS1​)
Words: 50
Variation of Hodge structure OurBigBook.com
In a variation of Hodge structure, differentiation lowers the filtration index by at most one. In the relative de Rham construction, an absolute form of degree at least p contributes, after extracting one base differential, a relative form of degree at least p−1. This filtration shift proves the condition for geometric variations.
Gauss–Manin connection (∇:H→H⊗ΩS1​)
Words: 42
Variation of Hodge structure OurBigBook.com
The flat connection on the complexified fibre-cohomology local system differentiates cohomology classes using topological parallel transport. For a smooth proper holomorphic family, relative de Rham cohomology identifies it with the connecting morphism obtained by retaining one base differential in the absolute de Rham complex.

Polarized Hodge structure ((−1)w(w−1)/2ip−qQ(v,vˉ)>0)

Words: 258 Articles: 4
Hodge structure OurBigBook.com
A polarization is a nondegenerate integral bilinear form of symmetry (−1)w, orthogonal on Hodge summands except complementary bidegrees, satisfying the displayed positivity for every nonzero v∈Hp,q. This convention takes the cup-product pairing as the primitive geometric polarization. Omitting the constant sign factor and rescaling Q is an equivalent convention. The full intersection pairing of a K3 surface is not itself a polarization: its real (1,1) space has one positive direction as well as nineteen negative directions.
Period domain (D⊆Dˇ)
Words: 181 Articles: 3
Polarized Hodge structure OurBigBook.com
Fix a lattice, a bilinear polarization and Hodge numbers. The period domain consists of the Hodge filtrations with these dimensions satisfying orthogonality, opposition and positivity. It is an open subset of its compact dual of a period domain, described algebraically by the dimensions and orthogonality conditions alone.
K3 period domain ({[ω]:q(ω,ω)=0, q(ω,ωˉ)>0})
Words: 62
Period domain OurBigBook.com
On the K3 intersection lattice, this open quadric has complex dimension twenty and records the period line H2,0. Fixing a positive class h of type (1,1) adds q(h,ω)=0 and yields a nineteen-dimensional domain for primitive polarized cohomology of signature (2,19). The distinction is necessary: the unrestricted full lattice has signature (3,19) and does not satisfy polarization positivity on all of H1,1.
Siegel upper half-space (Hr​={Z=ZT:ImZ>0})
Words: 39
Period domain OurBigBook.com
Positive complex Lagrangian subspaces for the integral symplectic form (0I​−I0​) are graphs HZ​={(Zu,u):u∈Cr}. Isotropy is the symmetry of Z, and iQ(v,vˉ)=2uT(ImZ)uˉ gives positivity. For g=(AC​BD​) in the symplectic group, the action is Z↦(AZ+B)(CZ+D)−1.
Compact dual of a period domain (Dˇ)
Words: 40
Period domain OurBigBook.com
The compact dual is the complex projective flag variety imposing prescribed filtration dimensions and Q(Fp,Fw−p+1)=0, but neither real opposition nor positivity. In weight one it is the complex Lagrangian Grassmannian. In polarized K3 weight two it is an isotropic-line quadric.

Hodge filtration (Fp=⨁r≥p​Hr,w−r)

Words: 30
Hodge structure OurBigBook.com
A decreasing filtration defines a Hodge structure when HC​=Fp⊕Fw−p+1 for every p. The decomposition is recovered as Hp,q=Fp∩Fq. This filtration is the holomorphic datum that varies in a variation of Hodge structure.

Jet bundle of maps (Jk(M,N))

Words: 58
Differential geometry OurBigBook.com
The space of Taylor-equivalence classes jxk​f of smooth maps Mm→Nn, with derivatives through order k agreeing at the source point. The projection jxk​f↦(x,f(x)) has total dimension m+n(km+k​) and fiber dimension n((km+k​)−1). Finite-dimensional broken-geodesic models prove the assertion at bounded energy, and exhaustion gives the full path space. On Sn with distinct nonantipodal endpoints the cell dimensions are j(n−1), one in each such dimension.

An oriented atlas is a smooth atlas whose smooth transition maps have positive Jacobian determinants on every overlap. The coordinate bases then give compatible choices of orientation of a vector space on all tangent spaces. A nowhere-vanishing top-degree differential form gives such an atlas: restrict each chart until its coefficient has constant sign, reverse one coordinate if necessary to make that sign positive, and compare the positive coefficients on overlaps. Conversely, a partition of unity glues positive local coordinate top forms to a global volume form.

For a smooth n-manifold, the following are equivalent: an atlas with positive transition Jacobians, a smooth choice of orientation of every tangent space, and a nowhere-vanishing smooth n-form. Local isometry

Words: 418 Articles: 8
First fundamental form OurBigBook.com
A local isometry between Riemannian manifolds is a local diffeomorphism f with f∗gN​=gM​. Equivalently, its differentials are isometric linear isomorphisms between tangent spaces. It preserves the Levi-Civita connection, intrinsic sectional curvature, and affinely parametrized geodesics. A map whose differentials are merely isometric injections is an isometric immersion; the local diffeomorphism requirement distinguishes these notions.

Local isometries are determined by first-order data

Local isometry OurBigBook.com
Two local isometries from a connected Riemannian manifold that have the same value and differential at one point agree everywhere. They preserve geodesics, so their equality follows on a normal neighborhood from f(expp​v)=expf(p)​(dfp​v). The set of points where both value and differential agree is consequently open, and continuity makes it closed. Connectedness completes the argument.

Complete local isometry is a covering

Words: 94
Local isometry OurBigBook.com
A local isometry from a nonempty complete Riemannian manifold to a connected Riemannian manifold is a surjective covering map. Lift radial geodesics in a normal ball using completeness; the exponential map at each inverse-image centre maps a tangent ball diffeomorphically onto a sheet. Uniqueness of the geodesic initial-value problem makes these sheets disjoint and exhaustive. Surjectivity follows by lifting piecewise geodesic paths. Conversely a Riemannian covering of a complete target is complete, by lifting complete target geodesics and using the Hopf-Rinow theorem. If the target is disconnected, the first assertion gives a covering only of the union of components met by the map.

Parity of real projective plane-curve intersections (∣Z(f)∩Z(g)∣≡ab(mod2))
Words: 92
Real projective plane OurBigBook.com
A degree-a homogeneous real polynomial defines a section of the ath tensor power of the dual real tautological line bundle over RP2. Its first Stiefel–Whitney class is au, where u generates H1(RP2;F2​). By parity of zeros of a real line-bundle section, a generic zero curve has mod-two dual class au. Two transverse zero curves of degrees a,b therefore have intersection parity ⟨abu2,[RP2]2​⟩=ab, since two distinct projective lines intersect once. For example, the line z=0 and the conic x2+y2−z2=0 are disjoint in the real projective plane, although their degree product is two.
Integral homology of two real projective planes (H∗​(RP2×RP2;Z))
Words: 65
Real projective plane OurBigBook.com
Each real projective plane has cells e0​,e1​,e2​ with de2​=2e1​ and de1​=0. Their product cellular chain complex has ranks 1,2,3,2,1. Its degree-two cycle e1​×e1​ has order two in homology. The degree-three cycle e2​×e1​+e1​×e2​ also has order two, because its double is d(e2​×e2​). Consequently H0​=Z, H1​=(Z/2)2, H2​=H3​=Z/2 and all other groups vanish. The degree-three torsion is also the Tor functor term in the Künneth theorem.
Metric on the antipodal sphere quotient (d([u],[v])=min(∥u−v∥,∥u+v∥))
Words: 48
Real projective plane OurBigBook.com
The displayed metric on antipodal classes of the unit sphere induces its quotient topology. Triangle inequality follows by choosing the signs that realize each minimum and applying the Euclidean triangle inequality. Distinct classes have disjoint saturated unions of small balls, proving the quotient is Hausdorff; compactness follows from the continuous quotient map.

Dirichlet energy

Words: 44
Differential geometry OurBigBook.com
The Dirichlet energy of a differentiable scalar function is one half the integral of its squared gradient. On a Euclidean domain it is E(u)=21​∫∣∇u∣2dx; the Dirichlet energy on a Riemannian manifold uses its metric and volume measure. Its stationary functions satisfy the Laplace equation with fixed boundary values.

Fundamental theorem of curves

Words: 53
Differential geometry OurBigBook.com
Suitable curvature functions determine a regular Frenet curve up to a Euclidean rigid motion. In the plane one signed curvature suffices; in three dimensions positive curvature and torsion determine a unit-speed curve, as in the fundamental theorem of regular space curves. The result is local on the parameter interval and assumes the regularity needed by the frame equations.
